paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens categorized into different clinical specialties between a baseline model, Mistralv0.2-Base, and the same model fine-tuned on various specialty data. The horizontal axis contains the categories of per-specialty terms labeled as Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, with no apparent order or scale type indicated. The vertical axis represents the negative log probability, labeled with values ranging from -27 to -22, with a linear scale and no units provided; tick labels are regularly spaced at intervals of 1. Each category on the horizontal axis contains a group of bars, with each group consisting of bars colored according to the legend: blue for Mistralv0.2-Base and shades of orange and brown for the model fine-tuned on Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, respectively. The blue bar for Mistralv0.2-Base has approximate values of -26 for Cardio, -25.5 for Gastro, -25.7 for Infect, -25.3 for Neuro, -25.7 for Obstetrics, and -25.3 for Pediatrics. The bars for the fine-tuned models within each specialty category have varying lengths, with some showing slightly higher or lower negative log-probabilities; for example, the fine-tuned model on Cardio has approximate values ranging from -23.3 to -22.8 across the different per-specialty terms. The bars within each group are not sorted in a specific way, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding according to the fine-tuning specialty data.
